subject: storytime
title: Town Mouse, Country Mouse
about: Aesop's fable of the country mouse who goes to town with the town mouse, enjoys a fancy feast until a big dog sends them running to hide, and decides his quiet home is best; in this telling nobody gets hurt. It gives first graders two very different settings to compare and a gentle lesson about what makes a home feel good. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, four pages long.
tip: Ask: would you rather live in a busy town or on a quiet farm, and why?

book.author: Aesop (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: Two mice, two very different homes, and one big dog.

passage.text:
Country Mouse lived on a farm.
His home was a little hole under a tree.
It was quiet and calm.
He ate seeds and nuts and corn.
One day, Town Mouse came to visit.
She looked at his food.
"Just seeds and nuts?" she said.
"Come to town with me."
"In town, we eat cake and cheese!"
***
So the two mice went to town.
Town Mouse lived in a big house.
Bang, clang, honk!
Town was very loud.
On the table was a feast.
There was cake and cheese and jam.
"Yum!" said Country Mouse.
The two mice began to eat.
***
Then a big dog ran in.
"Ruff! Ruff!"
"Run!" said Town Mouse.
The mice ran and hid in a hole.
They shook and shook.
At last the dog went away.
The mice were safe.
But Country Mouse did not want more cake.
***
"Is it always like this?" asked Country Mouse.
"Yes," said Town Mouse.
"Then I will go home," said Country Mouse.
"I like my seeds and nuts."
"I like my quiet home."
So he went back to his farm.
He ate his corn and slept well.
A calm, simple home can be best.

cards.q: Who lived in a big house in town?
cards.note: A town is a busy place with lots of houses, people and noise.

cards.q: What did Country Mouse eat at home?
cards.note: Plain farm food, but he liked it; the cake and cheese were in town.

cards.q: Who ran in while the mice were eating?
cards.note: Ruff, ruff: in this telling the mice just run and hide, and nobody gets hurt.

cards.q: What did the mice do when the dog came?
cards.note: They hid in a hole and stayed there until the dog went away.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: The visit to the farm comes first, then the trip to town, then the dog.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: He picked his quiet farm over the cake and the noise.

cards.q: How did the mice feel when the dog ran in?
cards.note: They shook and shook, which is how he can tell they were scared even though the story never says it.
Country Mouse had plain food, but his home was calm, and that mattered more to him than cake.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'feast' mean?
cards.note: A feast is lots of good food all at once, like a big holiday dinner.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
